target: model/src/ZeroBased/Domain.fs bucket(); configurations.csv CFG-4/CFG-5; activity-loads-reference.csv
finding: The bucket rule maps any activity whose responsible_entity is 'sponsor' (or role 'sponsor') to SponsorOwned before checking classification, and sponsor_owned share is 0 in every configuration. Consequence: the IndependentAuth bucket is empty (no activity lands in it), AdminJudgment holds only 43 h, CFG-4 and CFG-5 produce byte-identical costs, and 'full administration incl. independent authorization' leaves 2,369 SponsorOwned hours (37% of all human hours) with the sponsor at $500M. These include OA-GRT-005 (1,050 h), OA-ACG-007 (212 h), OA-CHR-008 (138 h), OA-ACG-011 (102 h), OA-GRT-011 (54 h), OA-CMP-004 (40 h), OA-ACG-002/008 (58 h), all of which a full-service administrator prepares or performs in practice; the sponsor keeps only the decision and sign-off.
evidence: activity-loads-reference.csv bucket totals: SponsorOwned 2,369 h, AdminJudgment 43 h, IndependentAuth 0 h; headline-scenarios.csv CFG-4 and CFG-5 identical at every AUA; CFG-5 description says vendor performs independent authorization.
proposed_correction: Split each sponsor-responsible activity into a vendor preparation part (bucket admin_judgment or independent_auth) and a reserved sponsor decision part (for example 70/30 for OA-GRT-005, 75/25 for OA-ACG-007 and OA-ACG-011, 100/0 for OA-CHR-008 verification and OA-ACG-002/008 preparation). Assert in tests that each bucket used by a configuration is non-empty and that CFG-4 differs from CFG-5.
estimated_impact: About +1,300 to +1,600 vendor hours at $500M (+2,500 h at $1B). That is roughly +1 OPS FTE and +0.2 to 0.3 FTE controller, or +$130k to $230k a year in View 1. Cash break-even at 20 bps moves from about $0.59B to about $0.7B to $0.8B.

target: model/src/ZeroBased/Workload.fs hoursByRole (authorizer); roles.csv authorizer/controller; headline-staffing.csv AUTH
finding: All second-person minutes go to the 'authorizer' role in the AUTH pool whatever the primary role is. The AUTH pool's 93.6 h is exactly OA-TEC-010 code review (60 h), OA-CMP-007 (19.2 h), OA-CMP-012 (12 h) and OA-CMP-021 (2.4 h). The vendor's financial authority therefore performs no financial authorization: vendor controller-role hours under CFG-5 at $500M are 4 h/yr (OA-CMP-022). Engineering code review is billed at $225/h controller rate, and nobody at the vendor owns sub-ledger close, reconciliation sign-off or manual-journal approval. Sponsor auditors relying on the SOC 1 would find nearly every financial control pushed to complementary user-entity controls.
evidence: Recompute: 300x40x0.3/60=60; 4x960x0.3/60=19.2; 20x120x0.3/60=12; 4x120x0.3/60=2.4; sum 93.6 = AUTH hours at every scale. activity-loads-reference.csv controller vendor hours = 4.
proposed_correction: Route second-person minutes to the pool of the primary role's independence peer: engineering review to ENG, policy to COMPLIANCE, financial to AUTH. Add a vendor controller ownership activity for DAF sub-ledger close, reconciliation sign-off and SOC 1 financial control ownership of at least 0.2 to 0.4 FTE per $500M under CFG-3 to CFG-5.
estimated_impact: Net +$35k to $75k a year: +0.2 to 0.4 FTE x $183k, less about $21k of misallocated AUTH cost moved to ENG.

target: model/src/ZeroBased/Staffing.fs minNamed/backupCost; parameters.csv ZBP-020 backup_retainer_hours, ZBP-042; data/evidence/activity-inventory-notes.md section 4
finding: The model's own evidence notes say that the reserved-authority coverage (CNV-GOV-004), the three-distinct-person release (CNV-GOV-003) and the out-of-chain reconciler set a per-sponsor headcount floor of about 2.5 FTE that is not an activity. Staffing.fs enforces only 2 named persons per pool, and the missing backup costs 40 h x pool rate (about $2.8k for OPS). A backup who keeps payment-initiation access, is trained on each release and covers 25 absence days plus December cannot be retained for 40 h a year. BackupCash is $12.8k to $15.6k in every scenario.
evidence: activity-inventory-notes.md section 4 'The staffing floor is not an activity... about 2.5 FTE'; headline-scenarios.csv backup_cash 12,800-15,600; ZBP-020 base 40 h.
proposed_correction: Add an explicit per-sponsor control-coverage floor when vendor_runs_controls (CFG-3 to CFG-5) and raise backup readiness to 100 to 200 h per backup person, covering quarterly practice runs, release training and absence cover.
estimated_impact: Backup readiness +$15k to $40k a year. If even 1 FTE of the 2.5 FTE floor falls on the vendor under CFG-5: +$110k to $180k per sponsor.

target: configurations.csv column 'external' (0 in all configs); activity-loads-reference.csv OA-CON-005, OA-GRT-012, OA-GRT-013, OA-CON-003
finding: External-bucket activities have vendor share 0 in every configuration, so their human exception minutes are counted as sponsor work. Custodians do not attribute DTC securities receipts to donor funds, and banks do not decide positive-pay or ACH-return exceptions: the administrator does. Under CFG-5 this work belongs to vendor OPS/FINANCE.
evidence: Reference run sponsor-borne External hours: OA-CON-005 75.6 h, OA-GRT-013 79.2 h, OA-GRT-012 58.1 h, OA-CON-003 7.7 h (221 h).
proposed_correction: Treat the exception-handling minutes of EXTERNAL-PROVIDER rows as AdminException, and leave only the provider fee (external_cost_per_event) as external.
estimated_impact: +221 vendor h at $500M and about +440 h at $1B under CFG-3 to CFG-5, or +$17k to $45k a year.

target: model/src/ZeroBased/Simulation.fs rawWeight; parameters.csv ZBP-010/ZBP-011; OA-CON-004, OA-CON-005, OA-CON-009, OA-ACG-009
finding: December demand is a flat monthly weight (3.5x) spread evenly across the month. In practice 40-50% of December contributions, and most securities transfers, arrive in the last 8 to 10 business days before a hard 31 December receipt-date cutoff. In the same window, unidentified DTC transfers without a letter of instruction rise from about 4-8% to 15-30%. There is also no January profile for acknowledgment corrections, valuation reissues, year-end statements and the resulting contacts.
evidence: rawWeight: 'year_end' returns season_dec_weight for every December day; there is no intra-month or January term. OA-CON-005 exception 0.08 and OA-CON-004 0.04 are flat all year.
proposed_correction: Add a last-two-weeks December multiplier (8 to 12x), a January 'tax_season' profile for OA-CON-009 exceptions, OA-ACG-009 and OA-ACN-008, and a seasonal exception-rate multiplier (2 to 3x in December) for OA-CON-004 and OA-CON-005. Re-run the simulation SLA test against the 31 December cutoff.
estimated_impact: OPS/FINANCE surge hours x2 to 3 (+100 to 250 h); possibly a second dedicated OPS hire earlier than 3,500 accounts; +$15k to $60k a year.

target: operational-activities.csv OA-ACN-008 (freq_base 0.5; exception_base 0.8)
finding: 0.4 human-handled donor/advisor contacts per account per year is low for a HNW/advisor-intermediated book. National sponsors typically see 1 to 2 contacts per account per year, concentrated in November to January. Even with 40-50% AI containment that leaves 0.6 to 1.0 human contacts per account.
evidence: Reference run: 1,000 events, 800 human, 193 h at 2,000 accounts. Evidence source is an assumption ('min-touch 1').
proposed_correction: Base freq 1.2 to 1.5 per account and exception rate 0.5 to 0.6, with a January peak profile.
estimated_impact: At 4,000 accounts: about 450 h to 700-1,100 h, or +$20k to $55k a year in Support.

target: operational-activities.csv OA-GRT-005 (exception_base 0.09; minutes_base 42)
finding: OA-GRT-005 is the single largest activity: 24% of all minutes in the inventory and 1,050 h at $500M. Once OA-GRT-004 and OA-CHR-002 run deterministic eligibility and status checks, a residual manual-review rate of 9% at 42 unaided minutes is conservative. Automated sponsors run about 3-6% manual review, and the median case (church, school, government unit or fiscal-sponsor confirmation) takes 15-25 min. Only the rare reserved A4 cases take an hour or more.
evidence: activity-inventory-notes.md top-15 table, rank 1 (EV-E10 touch rate 9% x 42 min, both unmeasured).
proposed_correction: Model a two-tier distribution: about 4% routine at 18 min plus about 0.5% reserved at 60 to 90 min. Calibrate on the CNV-ECO-003 shadow replay.
estimated_impact: At $500M: 1,050 h to 250-420 h, or -$45k to $75k a year. Currently that saving is sponsor labour value; after the bucket fix it is vendor cost.

target: operational-activities.csv OA-COM-004/007/009/010/011, OA-ACG-006; parameters.csv ZBP-023 new_sponsor_share
finding: Onboarding is annualised at 0.2 new sponsors a year, which turns about 1,150 h of implementation, migration, payee verification, hypercare and calibration (OA-COM-007 500 h, OA-COM-009 367 h, OA-ACG-006 100 h, OA-COM-011 69 h, OA-COM-010 50 h, OA-COM-004 60 h) into about 230 h of steady load. Two problems. The work is lumpy: it lands in a single 4 to 9 month window, often overlapping a December. The hours are also low for converting a $250M-$500M book from an incumbent system, which means cost basis, grant history, recurring and future-dated grants, successor designations, documents and parallel runs. In my experience that is 1,500 to 3,000 h.
evidence: activity-loads-reference.csv: OA-COM-007 events 0.2 (85 h), OA-COM-009 events 0.2 (62 h).
proposed_correction: Add an onboarding-year scenario that staffs the full onboarding hours inside the window, using contract implementation at $120/h. Raise the migration and implementation base to 1,500 to 2,500 h per mid-size sponsor and amortise it over the contract term (ZBP-039).
estimated_impact: Onboarding year +$150k to $350k. Amortised steady-state +$30k to $70k a year per sponsor.

target: model/src/ZeroBased/Staffing.fs staffPool mode selection; roles.csv compliance; headline-staffing.csv COMPLIANCE
finding: Pools below 0.6 FTE are forced to fractional mode regardless of cost. Compliance at $500M costs 794 h x $190 x 1.1 = $165.9k, against $121.8k for a dedicated compliance FTE. The role is also mis-graded: most compliance hours are analyst work (OA-CMP-029 corpus maintenance 96 h, OA-CHR-003 revalidation exceptions 53 h, OA-CMP-024 vendor SOC reviews 61 h, OA-CMP-032 48 h, part of OA-CMP-011 testing) priced at a fractional CCO rate.
evidence: headline-staffing.csv 500M CFG-5 COMPLIANCE fractional cost 165,851; roles.csv compliance dedicated base 121,842; at $100M: 664 h costs $138.9k.
proposed_correction: Choose min(fractional cost, dedicated cost) in staffPool, and split compliance into a fractional officer (150 to 250 h at $190) and an analyst ($55 to 75/h, or OPS-pool staff independent of payment initiation).
estimated_impact: -$40k to $80k a year at $100M to $1B.

target: model/src/ZeroBased/Analysis.fs line ~69 (charity upkeep); beneficium-scenarios.csv; fixed-costs.csv FC-008
finding: View 1 adds $86.3k 'charity data upkeep', of which $76.6k is labour (0.46 FTE at BNP-040/041 rates) plus $9k counsel, as separate cash. But the ENG pool already pays 2 dedicated engineers (about 3,055 productive h) for about 1,408 residual h at $500M, so about 1,600 h are idle. The upkeep tasks also overlap workload rows OA-CHR-003, OA-CHR-004, OA-CHR-010 and OA-CMP-008, and the counsel overlaps FC-008 'regulatory questions'.

target: fixed-costs.csv FC-001, FC-002, FC-003
finding: The insurance premiums ($15k cyber, $12k tech E&O, $8k crime) are consistent with about $1M-2M limits. Institutional sponsors with $0.5B-1B AUA, a vendor that generates ACH files (TPSP) and daily grant batches will contractually require $5M-10M cyber and E&O limits, plus crime cover that includes third-party/client property and social-engineering funds-transfer fraud at limits comparable to the largest daily batch. Nothing links limits to AUA or batch size.
evidence: FC-001..003 evidence_class ASSUMPTION, 'No quote'; ZBP-033 platform_creates_ach_files=1 activates FC-003.
proposed_correction: Specify contractual limits per tier and price a $5M tower. Base about $45k-90k for cyber plus E&O and $15k-35k for crime, with a step at $1B AUA.
estimated_impact: +$25k to $80k a year.

target: fixed-costs.csv FC-004, FC-005; operational-activities.csv OA-TEC-020, OA-CMP-011
finding: The SOC fees ($27.5k SOC 2 and $44.5k SOC 1) are compliance-automation marketplace vendor claims. Sponsor auditors at national charities, who rely on the SOC 1 for contribution, grant and valuation assertions, commonly expect a recognised CPA firm, and a combined SOC 1 + SOC 2 Type II over a payments-and-ledger system typically runs $70k-150k plus bridge letters. Internal effort OA-TEC-020 of 80 h a year is also light: about 300-500 h in year 1 and 150-250 h at steady state.
evidence: FC-004/005 source 'vendor claims not quotes'; OA-TEC-020 1 x 4,800 min.
proposed_correction: Quote a recognised firm and raise OA-TEC-020 to 150-250 h. Consider a combined SOC 1/SOC 2 engagement, which can save 15-25% of fees.
estimated_impact: Fees +$20k to $60k; internal effort +70 to 170 compliance h (+$15k to $35k).

target: fixed-costs.csv FC-102 (allocated) vs View 1; FC-202
finding: The vendor's own accounting is missing from cash. FC-102 is 'allocated' (View 2 only), yet the evidence says no Echelon accounting function exists, and Unbound would be the only revenue-generating product. Bookkeeping, revenue recognition for bps billing in arrears (ZBP-040), payroll for 2-5 employees, tax filings, and the reviewed or audited vendor financial statements that institutional DDQs (OA-COM-002/003) ask for to show vendor viability are all incremental cash caused by Unbound.
evidence: FC-102 rationale 'No Echelon accounting function exists'; view=allocated, allocation_share 0.25.
proposed_correction: Add an incremental line: outsourced bookkeeping, payroll and tax at $15k-30k, plus a financial statement review or audit at $15k-40k once the first sponsor is live.
estimated_impact: +$30k to $70k a year in View 1.

target: operational-activities.csv OA-TEC-018, OA-TEC-010; parameters.csv ZBP-043 min_named_engineering
finding: There are segregation-of-duties gaps in engineering. OA-TEC-018 (workforce access recertification) is performed by engineering, which means the engineers review their own privileged access. CNV-PLT-010 requires two non-author approvers, but only one 30% second-person share is costed, and it goes to AUTH (see ADV-OC-002). The third named engineer is the founder with about 230-370 h a year, so founder unavailability stops control-relevant releases and leaves 2 people who can collude on payment-file code with production access.
evidence: OA-TEC-018 human_role engineering; Workload.fs authMinutes = human x minutes x 0.3 (one reviewer); headline-staffing.csv ENG founder_hours 314 (228.6 at $1B).
proposed_correction: Move access recertification and privileged-activity log review to compliance or controller (+40-60 h). Cost two reviewer passes for OA-TEC-010 in ENG (+120 h). Add a named non-founder third approver, or a contracted reviewer retainer.
estimated_impact: +$15k to $40k a year (reviewer retainer plus hours). Main effect is credibility at the SOC 1/SOC 2 walkthrough.

target: operational-activities.csv OA-TEC-001/003/004, OA-CMP-021 (SLA 1 h), OA-CMP-017 (SLA 4 h); Staffing.fs minNamed COMPLIANCE=1
finding: Activities with a 1-hour SLA require 24x7 on-call. Two engineers plus the founder means each person is on call one week in three, with no on-call allowance costed. Fraud/account-takeover triage (OA-CMP-017, 4 h SLA) and sanctions dispositions sit with a single named fractional compliance person: in December, or when that person is absent, the SLA cannot be met and nobody else is authorised to dispose.
evidence: minNamed: 'COMPLIANCE' | 'COMM' -> 1.0; FC-009 covers paging tooling only.
proposed_correction: Add an on-call allowance ($8k-15k per engineer) and require 2 named compliance persons with a backup retainer.
estimated_impact: +$20k to $45k a year.

target: model/src/ZeroBased/Analysis.fs lines 36-40 (seeded incidents); parameters.csv ZBP-024..031; OA-TEC-002, OA-TEC-004, OA-TEC-012/013
finding: Incident hours are counted twice. The simulation adds seeded security incidents (1/yr x 24 h ENG + 8 h OPS), integration failures (6/yr x 8 h ENG + 4 h OPS) and operational failures (4/yr x 8 h FINANCE) on top of activity rows that already carry the same work: OA-TEC-004 security incident response (4/yr x 25 h), OA-TEC-002 operational incident response (50 h per sponsor), and OA-TEC-012/013 integration maintenance and file exceptions. This also inflates the simulated peak FTE that drives the second engineer.
evidence: Staffing.fs adds incident hours to pool hours; activity rows also present in activity-loads-reference.csv.
proposed_correction: Use one representation: either the seeded incidents (for timing) with the activity rows' annual hours reduced, or the activity rows alone.
estimated_impact: -40 to 120 h a year (-$5k to $15k). It may also lower simulated ENG peak FTE from 1.55.

target: fixed-costs.csv FC-008 recurring legal counsel; FC-304
finding: Recurring counsel at 50 h ($22.5k) is thin for a full administrator. It has multi-year administration agreements, an ODFI/TPSP agreement, state data-breach notification analysis, AG and regulator inquiry support (OA-CMP-028 is sponsor-led but the vendor must respond), and policy-pack legal review (OA-CMP-007). It also conflicts with DF-ASR-2026-0D0F (no counsel spend), so the base case relies on spend the owner has not authorised.
evidence: FC-008 '20/50/120 h x $450/h'; rationale notes open conflict.
proposed_correction: Base 100-150 h, plus a contingent line for incident and regulatory matters. Resolve the owner-decision conflict before publishing the break-even.
estimated_impact: +$20k to $50k a year.

target: operational-activities.csv OA-GRT-016, OA-INV-011, OA-INV-010; activity-inventory-notes.md section 4
finding: Several recurring activities are missing or understated. Multi-state unclaimed-property holder reporting and due-diligence letters (an annual filing calendar, not per-grant touches inside OA-GRT-016). Fee billing disputes and fee reversals. Information returns for advisor fees paid from funds (1099-NEC/MISC for OA-INV-011 advisor programmes). Donor annual giving or tax summaries. Grant agreements and conditional grants (listed as an uncovered gap).
evidence: OA-GRT-016 is per_grant 1% x 19 min, with no per-state filing driver; no fee-dispute or information-return row in the 180 activities.
proposed_correction: Add per-sponsor annual rows: escheat filings 20-40 h, fee disputes 0.002 per account x 30 min, information returns 10-20 h, annual summary exceptions.
estimated_impact: +40 to 120 h a year per sponsor (+$4k to $12k).

target: operational-activities.csv OA-ACN-013 (25 min), OA-ACN-014 (60 min)
finding: Death and succession minutes are low. A typical successor case involves chasing documents (death certificate, letters testamentary), dealing with multiple successors, splitting funds, new agreements and identity proofing for each successor, and takes 3 to 6 hours including correspondence. Notification lag also creates backlogs of dormant deceased-holder accounts, which surface during dormancy outreach (OA-ACN-016).
evidence: OA-ACN-014 is 1% of accounts at 60 min, classified sponsor; OA-ACN-013 is 2% at 25 min.
proposed_correction: Raise OA-ACN-014 to 180-300 min with vendor preparation, and add a one-off backlog-review allowance at migration.
estimated_impact: +60 to 200 h a year at 2,000-4,000 accounts (+$5k to $15k).

target: data/evidence/activity-inventory-notes.md section 6; OA-CMP-003, OA-ACG-005, OA-ACG-007, OA-INV-004, OA-CMP-016
finding: Some inherited requirements create redundant work, and the register keeps all of it at full cost. There are three overlapping sampling regimes over the same decisions (OA-CMP-003, decision-quality sampling, and sampled reviews in OA-CMP-004). Reconciliation assurance is layered three times (OA-ACG-005 attestation, OA-ACG-007 controller sign-off, and CNV-GOV-003). A daily independent NAV sample (OA-INV-004, 50% x 250 days) checks values Unbound does not compute, and there is an annual affiliation attestation for every account (OA-CMP-016). The model's own notes identify these, but the inputs still apply them.
evidence: activity-inventory-notes.md section 6 items 1-4; OA-INV-004 freq 250 x 0.5 x 10 min = 20.8 h per sponsor.
proposed_correction: Use one error-bound sampling plan, weekly or risk-triggered NAV sampling, and event-driven affiliation confirmation, and reduce the corresponding rows.
estimated_impact: -40 to 90 h a year per sponsor (-$5k to $15k). Mostly sponsor-side now, vendor-side after ADV-OC-001.

target: data/model-outputs/baseline-comparison.csv; results.md section 3 break-even; headline-scenarios.csv sponsor_hours/sponsor_labour_value
finding: The break-even comparison ($0.5B-0.6B cash against the original $1.92B) assumes the same 20 bps fee while CFG-5 leaves 2,631 h (at $500M) and 5,189 h (at $1B) of administration with the sponsor. That is about 1.7 to 3.4 FTE plus the reserved-authority floor, which the sponsor must still staff. A sponsor paying 20 bps for 'full administration' would not accept that, so either the fee or the vendor scope is mis-stated. The sponsor labour value ($184k at $500M, $363k at $1B at $70/h) is reported but excluded from every view and from break-even.
evidence: headline-scenarios.csv CFG-5: sponsor_hours 2,630.8 / 5,189.0; sponsor_labour_value 184,155 / 363,233; break-even uses view1 to view3 only.
proposed_correction: Report break-even on vendor cost at like-for-like scope (after the ADV-OC-001 fix), and show a 'sponsor total cost of ownership' view equal to the vendor fee plus sponsor labour value, so the 20 bps price can be tested against the incumbent.
estimated_impact: Moving the delegable hours to the vendor adds about $130k-230k (ADV-OC-001). On a like-for-like basis cash break-even rises to about $0.7B-0.8B. That still beats $1.92B, but the advantage is about 40% smaller than headlined.

target: fixed-costs.csv FC-012 (activation not_standalone); FC-206
finding: CFG-7 (standalone administrator) drops the sales and marketing programme (FC-012 activation 'not_standalone') with no standalone replacement, so CFG-7 View 1 comes out $25k below CFG-5 ($1.092M against $1.117M at $500M). A standalone company has more need for marketing, not less. D&O insurance appears only inside FC-206 (View 3), even though institutional sponsors' DDQs ask about D&O for any administrator.
evidence: headline-scenarios.csv AUA 500M: CFG-7 view1 1,092,454 vs CFG-5 1,117,454; difference = FC-012 base 25,000.
proposed_correction: Change FC-012 activation to 'always', or add a standalone marketing line. Consider a small D&O line in View 1 for CFG-5 and CFG-7.
estimated_impact: +$25k CFG-7 View 1; D&O +$5k to $15k.

target: data/model-outputs/infrastructure.csv column ai; operational-activities.csv OA-TEC-021 and AI-ASSISTED rows
finding: Infrastructure prices AI usage at about $24 a year for 1,000 accounts ($193 at 10,000). The design relies on AI for grounded donor answers (OA-ACN-001), exception preparation, the monthly close package (OA-ACG-007), the Form 990 package (OA-ACG-010), and an agent evaluation and change-control regime (OA-TEC-021, 384 h a year), which implies recurring evaluation-suite runs. Model-usage cost for evaluations and agent runs is plausibly two orders of magnitude higher.
evidence: infrastructure.csv C1,1000: ai 23.6565; FC-104 notes 'agent usage cost unmeasured'.
proposed_correction: Add a fixed AI evaluation and agent-usage floor of $3k-15k a year, and meter it in the pilot.
estimated_impact: +$3k to $15k a year.
